subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Bandwidth: The Speed Limit of a Channel
description: A 60-second lesson on Bandwidth: The Speed Limit of a Channel.

hook.text: Bandwidth is the range of frequencies a channel can carry. Wider is faster.

buildup.text: A telephone line passes 300 to 3,400 Hz — enough for voice, not for music.

discovery.text: Shannon's theorem: maximum data rate equals bandwidth × log₂(1 + SNR). A hard limit.

twist.text: You can't beat Shannon's limit. More bandwidth or better SNR are the only ways to go faster.

climax.text: 5G uses millimeter-wave bands — huge bandwidth for gigabit speeds, but short range.

punchline.text: Wider pipe, more data — bandwidth is the speed limit physics imposes.

quiz.question: According to Shannon's theorem, what two factors determine maximum data rate?
options: Voltage and current of the signal
Frequency and wavelength of the carrier
